channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Bruce Springsteen quer entender eleitor de Trump
item.description: Bruce Springsteen said he wants to find 'common ground' with a portion of his audience that distanced itself from him due to his political stances, particularly regarding Trump voters. He made the comment at the 2026 Tribeca Film Festival while receiving the Harry Belafonte Voices for Social Justice Award. Springsteen aims to reconnect with fans who felt alienated by his activism.

item.title: Renan surfa eleitor 'nem-nem' que Caiado e Zema esnobaram
item.description: Renan emerges as an alternative for 'neither-nor' voters (neither Bolsonaro supporters nor Lula supporters) who were overlooked by former governors Ronaldo Caiado (PSD-GO) and Romeu Zema (Novo-MG), who are trying to inherit Jair Bolsonaro's legacy without attracting this segment. While Caiado and Zema focus on appealing to the far right, Renan gains traction by addressing more moderate and pragmatic demands.

item.title: No Rio, Zema minimiza fala de Eduardo Bolsonaro sobre rompimento com o Novo e reafirma críticas a Flávio
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's pre-candidate for President, downplayed Eduardo Bolsonaro's claim of a 'general rupture' between the PL and Novo, stating the parties remain allied in several states. He reiterated his criticism of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's association with banker Daniel Vorcaro, calling him a 'bandit banker' and saying he never met with him. Zema added that the right will unite in a potential runoff against Lula, regardless of internal conflicts.

item.title: Condenação de Eduardo dói na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The likely conviction of Eduardo Bolsonaro by the Federal Supreme Court is negatively impacting the campaign of his brother, Flávio Bolsonaro, who is running for governor of Rio de Janeiro in 2026. A Quaest poll released on Monday shows that Eduardo’s verdict could harm Flávio’s image through association, despite no direct involvement in the alleged crimes. The question is no longer whether Eduardo will be convicted, but the severity of the sentence and its electoral consequences.

item.title: Zema é desconvidado de evento do Novo em SC
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for president under the Novo party, was uninvited from a Novo party event in Santa Catarina scheduled for July. The decision followed a public suggestion by former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL) that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro distance himself from Zema, amid criticisms made by the former governor. The incident highlights internal tensions between Bolsonaro allies and the Novo party regarding Zema’s political stance.

item.title: Moraes não é só vítima e juiz, mas também investigador, acusador e, às vezes, carcereiro
item.description: The text argues that Alexandre de Moraes holds conflicting roles in Brazil’s judicial system — as victim, investigator, accuser, judge, and sometimes jailer — raising concerns about impartiality, particularly in cases like Carla Zambelli’s extradition. It alleges his STF office informally requested reports from the TSE to justify pre-decided measures, involving aide Eduardo Tagliaferro, and notes that Italy’s Court of Cassation did not acquit Zambelli but rejected extradition due to objective concerns about Moraes’s impartiality.

item.title: Desconvite a Zema pelo Novo em SC desagrada sigla em MG: "Desrespeito"
item.description: Minas Gerais Novo Party president Christopher Laguna criticized Santa Catarina's Novo branch for withdrawing an invitation to former governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema, calling the move discourteous and unrepresentative of the national party. He attributed the decision to pro-Bolsonaro pressure within SC's directory, despite Zema's criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro. The SC directory defended the move as necessary to unite the right against Lula's re-election.

item.title: Presidente da bancada da bala apresenta moção de repúdio a Lula
item.description: Federal Deputy Alberto Fraga (PL-DF), president of the Parliamentary Front for Public Security, introduced a motion of repudiation against President Lula in the Chamber's Committee on Public Security and Combating Organized Crime, claiming Lula offended low-income populations. The move reflects ongoing tensions between the 'bancada da bala' and the federal government.

item.title: Daniella Marques vai integrar núcleo econômico de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Economist Daniella Marques, former president of Caixa Econômica Federal and former member of Paulo Guedes’ team in the Bolsonaro government, has been named part of the economic and social mobility core of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) presidential pre-campaign. The announcement was made at the Veja-promoted Fórum Rumos do Brasil in São Paulo, where Flávio praised her expertise and trustworthiness, particularly in economic inclusion and female entrepreneurship. Daniella confirmed her participation on social media, stating she accepted the role despite personal sacrifices, believing in a larger mission for Brazil’s future.

item.title: Zema é 'desconvidado' de evento do Novo em Santa Catarina após atritos do mineiro com o bolsonarismo
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's pre-candidate for president, was uninvited from a party event in Santa Catarina after publicly criticizing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) over his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master. The decision was made by Novo’s pre-candidates and mayors in SC, despite the PL-Novo alliance in the state. Zema said he wishes to return to the state and stands by his past criticisms, though he avoided new remarks on the matter.

item.title: Pesquisa inédita aponta que 7 em cada 10 brasileiros estão fora dos extremos políticos
item.description: A FESPSP study finds that 69% of Brazilians lack a 'love and hate' bond with political poles, showing growing indifference as the dominant sentiment. While ideological polarization rose from 19% in 2006 to 31% today, voters tend to reject opponents before positively aligning with any camp, with a 16-point drop in positive adhesion without hostility. Coordinator Jairo Pimentel warns that this cold or disenchanted relationship with politics weakens democratic representation.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que prevê novas regras para financiamento de transporte público urbano
item.description: President Lula sanctioned the new Legal Framework for Urban Collective Public Transportation, which establishes new rules for financing, contracting, and managing the sector, aiming to reduce reliance on passenger fares and tie operators’ remuneration to service performance and quality. The law enhances transparency by requiring disclosure of operational costs, revenue, passenger numbers, and performance indicators. Lula vetoed provisions mandating budget-funded gratuities, a five-year adaptation period, toll exemptions for buses, federal subsidies, and the use of carbon credits as financing, citing concerns over fiscal responsibility, federal autonomy, and legal certainty of contracts.

item.title: Lula tem encontros com presidentes da França e da Suíça
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva held bilateral meetings with Swiss President Guy Parmelin in Geneva and French President Emmanuel Macron in Évian, on the occasion of the G7 Summit. The discussions covered defense cooperation, artificial intelligence, energy, health, bilateral trade, and the Mercosul-EFTA agreement, alongside global issues such as reforming international governance and combating deforestation. Lula also highlighted the creation of Unitaid and France’s interest in supporting Brazil in supercomputing and cross-border cooperation between French Guiana and Amapá.

item.title: Nova taxação proposta pelos EUA pode impactar um terço das exportações brasileiras com tarifas de até 37,5%, projeta CNI
item.description: The CNI projects that proposed U.S. tariffs could affect 31.6% of Brazilian exports to the U.S. with a 37.5% duty, up from the current 10%, due to allegations of unfair trade practices and insufficient action against forced labor. The measure, still under public consultation, could impact up to 54.1% of exports when combined with existing Section 232 tariffs, with exceptions for strategic goods like beef and coffee. The Lula administration seeks to reverse the additional tariff through negotiations and is evaluating a potential meeting with Trump at the G7 summit in France.

item.title: Pesquisa indica busca por 3ª via em seu melhor momento e ameaça polarização PT-PL
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll reveals that 24% of Brazilian voters prefer a third-way presidential candidate in 2026, rejecting both Lula (PT) and Bolsonaro (PL), marking the highest level in the survey’s history. Lula rose to 42% in voting intentions against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), who fell to 33%, affected by the BolsoMaster scandal and new U.S. tariffs. Nevertheless, 25% of far-right voters say they would only support Flávio, highlighting enduring loyalty to Bolsonaro within the conservative base.

item.title: Deputado do PT propõe CPI para apurar contratos do programa Muralha Paulista
item.description: State Deputy Donato (PT) filed a request for a Parliamentary Inquiry Commission (CPI) in the São Paulo Legislative Assembly to investigate possible irregularities in the Muralha Paulista surveillance camera program under Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' administration. The investigation focuses on scrutinizing suspicious contracts related to the monitoring system.

item.title: Associações repudiam fala de Lula sobre população temer ir à delegacia por medo do 'tipo de policial' que vai encontrar
item.description: Police civil associations, including Adepol and Sindesp, repudiated President Lula's statement that Brazilians fear going to police stations due to uncertainty about the 'type of officer' they might encounter, calling it inadequate, unjust, and decontextualized. They argued that the comment fosters a generalized perception of distrust toward police institutions, which does not reflect reality, as procedures for seizing and holding stolen phones are legally established, formally documented, and subject to internal oversight and external control by the Judiciary and Public Ministry. Sindesp endorsed Adepol's statement, emphasizing the essential role of police delegates and civil officers in criminal investigations, property recovery, and public safety.

item.title: Renan ironiza possível escolha de Zanatta como vice de Flávio
item.description: Renan Santos, president of the Missão party and pre-candidate for Presidency, mocked the potential selection of federal deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) as Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) running mate, saying it makes victory too easy and that he wants to earn merit in winning. He shared a video posted by Zanatta to underscore his criticism.

item.title: Não é a direita, mas o bolsonarismo que, hoje, tende a perder para Lula
item.description: Recent polls show Lula leading the 2026 presidential race, with Bolsonarismo in decline despite resistance from sectors of the right. The monocratic suspension of an AtlasIntel poll by Supreme Court Justice Kassio Nunes Marques, acting as TSE president, sparked controversy by attempting to block the release of data showing Flávio Bolsonaro's decline. The article argues that the expected defeat is not of the right in general, but specifically of Bolsonarismo.

item.title: Lula e OMS assinam carta para que países concluam tratado sobre pandemias
item.description: President Lula and WHO Director-General Tedros signed an open letter during the G7 summit on June 15, 2026, urging international leaders to finalize the pandemic treaty, particularly the annex on Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing. The agreement, concluded in April 2025 after three years of negotiations, remains unratified due to this unresolved annex, which the signatories call the 'final piece' for the treaty to enter into force. The next negotiation round is scheduled for July 6–17, 2026.

item.title: Lula tem 35% contra 26% de Flávio entre eleitores năo polarizados, aponta pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: Lula leads with 35% of voting intentions among non-polarized voters, according to the BTG/Nexus poll, while Flávio Bolsonaro has 26%. The survey was released on Monday, the 15th, and reflects the broadest scenario for the first round of the 2026 elections.

item.title: 45% dos brasileiros têm uma imagem negativa de Trump
item.description: The negative image of U.S. President Donald Trump among Brazilians rose from 39% in May to 45% in June 2026, according to a Genial/Quaest poll. Meanwhile, unfavorable views of the U.S. reached 46%, and support for an independent stance toward the U.S. grew to 31%, while backing for an alliance fell to 46%. The survey, conducted June 5–8 with 2,004 respondents, has a 2-point margin of error and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: O que Sergio Moro diz sobre ligação de Flávio Bolsonaro com o Banco Master
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro avoided criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro over his links to Banco Master, stating he signed investigation requests and has no commitment to any form of misconduct. He noted the scandal occurred under Lula’s government, with the governing coalition consistently opposing investigations while the opposition, including Bolsonaro, supported them. Moro also criticized the lack of scrutiny on alleged irregularities involving Fábio Luís Lula da Silva.

item.title: Zema diz que seu aliado e sucessor privatizará a Cemig se for reeleito em MG
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) stated that his successor and ally, current Minas Gerais governor Mateus Simões (PSD), plans to privatize Cemig if re-elected, although Simões has been cautious on the issue so far. Zema made the remark at a Veja magazine event in São Paulo, noting his administration prioritized Copasa’s privatization, which generated R$ 8.4 billion. He also said he would privatize 'everything' if elected president to boost the economy.

item.title: A AGU prestes a ganhar mais poderes
item.description: Jorge Messias, awaiting his (re)nomination to the STF promised by Lula, is working to expand the powers of the Attorney General's Office (AGU). The article highlights his efforts to strengthen the AGU's role in Brazil's political and legal landscape, though it is available only to subscribers.

item.title: ‘Próxima pandemia não vai aguardar’: Lula e diretor da OMS fazem apelo por acordo
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus issued a joint appeal urging world leaders to accelerate the conclusion of an international pandemic prevention and response agreement, warning that 'the next pandemic will not wait for us'. They emphasized the need to finalize the annex on pathogen information sharing and equitable access to vaccines, tests, and treatments, citing the over US$13 trillion economic impact of Covid-19 and the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as urgent reminders of global unpreparedness.

item.title: Flávio: diferença entre roubo e latrocínio é uma “fração de segundo”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), senator and pre-candidate for President, stated that the difference between cellphone robbery and latrocínio (robbery followed by murder) is a 'fraction of a second', criticizing President Lula for alleged leniency toward criminals. He advocated for increased penalties, evaluation of criminal history in custody hearings, and the construction of 500,000 new prison spots, citing a current deficit of 298,875 vacancies and 161.7% overcrowding. He also reiterated that Lula does not classify PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, claiming the president 'defends the bandits'.

item.title: Alinhado com Lula, Motta contraria oposição e votará projeto que equipara misonigia ao racismo
item.description: Chamber President Hugo Motta announced he will vote to approve a bill equating misogyny with racism, aligning with President Lula’s agenda and responding to priorities of female voters. The measure, reported by PSB deputy Tabata Amaral, is set for a vote this week and is expected to further alienate the opposition, which has criticized Motta’s growing alignment with the government.

item.title: O erro que Flávio Bolsonaro aponta no governo de seu pai
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and pre-candidate for president, criticized his father Jair Bolsonaro's government for its adversarial relationship with the press, citing prejudice in public advertising budgets and restricted freedom of expression as key mistakes. He stated that, under his potential administration, press and expression freedom would be guaranteed regardless of critical coverage, emphasizing the need to learn from past errors and govern differently.

item.title: Renan Santos dispara no ‘Data-Toalha’
item.description: Renan Santos, founder of MBL and the Mission party, ranks third in some presidential vote intention polls, behind Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, but leads in the informal 'Data-Toalha' indicator, which tracks towel sales in São Paulo's Jardins neighborhood. Though not scientific, the metric reflects his growing appeal among conservative and upper-middle-class voters. The report was published by O Antagonista.

item.title: Para destrancar pauta da Câmara, Motta pautará mais um PL do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: Chamber President Hugo Motta announced he will put to vote this week the bill to end the 6×1 work schedule, aiming to unblock the House agenda. Although the constitutional amendment (PEC) on the same topic has advanced and is awaiting review in the Senate, the Lula government has not withdrawn the constitutional urgency from the bill, keeping the agenda locked. Motta said rapporteur Leo Prates will meet with party leaders on Tuesday to advance the vote.

item.title: A resposta de Flávio Bolsonaro a críticas ao Bolsa Família
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro defended the Bolsa Família program as an acquired right and rejected prejudices against its beneficiaries, stating that nearly 70% work informally. He proposed that those who secure formal employment or start a business should continue receiving the benefit for a longer period to encourage autonomy without political dependence. Currently, families with per capita income above R$706 receive half the benefit for up to 12 months before being phased out.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro defende Bolsa Família e isenção de IR até R$ 5.000
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) defended the continuity of Bolsa Família as an acquired right and proposed extending the protection period for beneficiaries who enter formal employment or start businesses, citing fear of losing benefits as a barrier to formalization. He also supported exempting Income Tax for earnings up to R$5,000, aligning with a campaign promise from former President Jair Bolsonaro, though without specifying funding mechanisms.

item.title: 'Parem de facilitar', ironiza Renan Santos após vídeo de Júlia Zanatta, cotada a vice de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate from the Missão party, criticized the potential nomination of Júlia Zanatta as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate, saying it would make victory too easy and diminish his merit. The suggestion came from Eduardo Bolsonaro, who praised Zanatta's loyalty, sparking a debate with Rodrigo Constantino. Zanatta defended her electoral value and questioned Romeu Zema's appeal as an alternative.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro defende classificação de milicianos como terroristas
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) advocated for classifying militias as narcoterrorist groups, aligning them with criminal factions like the Comando Vermelho and PCC, arguing they impose collective fear and extort taxes in communities. He stated that any criminal adopting practices similar to these factions should be labeled as terrorists, including militiamen. Although he has previously supported applying this classification to criminal factions, this is the first time he explicitly included militias in this category.

item.title: Moraes rejeita adiar ação penal contra Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes rejected the Public Defender's Office request to delay the criminal trial against Eduardo Bolsonaro, keeping the hearing scheduled for June 16, 2026. The ruling states that the 1st Chamber has the required quorum of at least three justices (currently four) and that any tie would benefit the defendant, causing no harm to the defense. The case stems from allegations that Eduardo Bolsonaro acted in the U.S. to pressure justices and interfere in the process that led to Jair Bolsonaro's conviction for attempted coup.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro confirma Daniella Marques na campanha para cuidar de propostas da área econômica
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed that Daniella Marques, former president of Caixa Econômica Federal and former advisor to Paulo Guedes, will assist in drafting economic and social proposals for his 2026 presidential pre-campaign, focusing on austerity, social responsibility, microcredit, and female entrepreneurship. Marques took a six-month leave from Legend to dedicate herself to the project and had already been informally advising the campaign.

item.title: Colírio para os olhos: veja fotos dos famosos nos estádios para a Copa do Mundo
item.description: The 2026 World Cup featured celebrity sightings including Tom Cruise, David Beckham, Victoria Beckham, Katy Perry, Justin Trudeau, Paris Hilton, Jason Sudeikis, Tom Brady, and Travis Scott at matches across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico. Cruise and Beckham drew attention at the U.S. vs. Paraguay opener, while Perry and Trudeau were seen sharing affection during the same game. In the Brazil vs. Morocco match in New Jersey, Brady and Scott were also spotted in the stands.

item.title: Senado terá sessões remotas e pauta esvaziada enquanto votação da PEC 6x1 segue indefinida
item.description: The Federal Senate will hold semi-presential voting sessions this week, allowing senators to participate remotely while they focus on pre-campaign activities in their home states. The agenda will be light, emphasizing consensus items such as the Sports University and the symbolic transfer of the capital to Salvador, while the vote on PEC 6x1 — which would end the 6x1 work schedule — remains undecided, with no rapporteur assigned and no clarity on whether it will proceed through committees or directly to the floor.

item.title: Michelle impõe condição a filhos de Bolsonaro para entrar na campanha de Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro has conditioned her involvement in Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign on a public apology from the former president’s sons. The demand was reported by PL leadership in an exclusive article. She seeks a symbolic gesture before committing to the 2026 election effort.

item.title: Lula se encontra com Macron durante cúpula do G7
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with French President Emmanuel Macron on the sidelines of the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, reaffirming Brazil's commitment to multilateralism and the voice of the Global South. Although no concrete meeting with Donald Trump is expected, Lula used the summit to oppose the potential U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods following a Section 301 investigation proposing a 25% duty. Lula also discussed critical minerals and AI with Switzerland’s president, while the G7 final communiqué is set to highlight the 'potential risks' of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Flávio defende Bolsa Família, isenção do IR para quem ganha até R$ 5 mil e diz que pai errou na relação com a imprensa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro defends Bolsa Família as an acquired right and proposes expanding its protection for beneficiaries who obtain formal employment or start a business, to prevent fear of losing benefits. He also supports income tax exemption for those earning up to R$ 5,000 and criticizes the strained relationship between his father’s government and the press, calling it a mistake that must be corrected.

item.title: Na véspera de julgamento de Eduardo Bolsonaro, Moraes nega pedidos da Defensoria
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes rejected the Public Defender's Office requests to postpone or reconvene Eduardo Bolsonaro's trial in the First Chamber of the STF, keeping the session scheduled for Tuesday. He stated that with four ministers present, the chamber meets the internal regency's minimum requirement of three, thus no violation of natural judge or collegiality principles occurred. Moraes also noted that a potential tie would benefit the defendant, as the criminal action concerns allegations of procedural coercion linked to Eduardo’s advocacy for U.S. sanctions against Brazil.

item.title: A estratégia de SP para acelerar a universalização dos serviços de água e esgoto
item.description: Following its privatization in August 2024, Sabesp accelerated the universalization target for water and sewage services from 2033 to 2029, backed by an annual investment of 369 reais per capita — above both national averages and the estimated minimum needed. In 2025, the company allocated 15.2 billion reais, its highest historical investment, a 120% increase from the pre-privatization year. Official data shows 87% water supply coverage, 77% sewage collection, and 71% sewage treatment progress for 2024–2026.

item.title: Caiado critica juros e diz que governo ‘enrolou a população’ antes do Desenrola
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized the Selic rate of 14.75% and accused the federal government of having 'misled the population' by encouraging consumption, production, and loans before launching the Desenrola debt renegotiation program. He questioned the logic of releasing savings to pay what he called 'loan-shark' interest rates, calling for clearer economic policies. The Desenrola 2.0 program has renegotiated R$20 billion in family debts, with 1.4 million agreements and an average discount of 85%, reducing the total owed to R$2.7 billion.

item.title: ‘Quem cobrava taxa das blusinhas eram os governadores’, diz Haddad no VEJA Fórum Rumos do Brasil
item.description: Former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad defended Lula's tax policy, stating that the so-called 'tax on small clothes' was initially proposed by governors and unanimously approved by Congress. He dismissed criticisms as 'smoke screens' and highlighted Brazil's economic progress, including the lowest inflation in four years, lowest unemployment in historical series, and best GDP growth since 2010, while emphasizing the country's leadership in clean energy and ecological transition.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que privatizações enfrentam barreira ideológica
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas argued that privatization debates in Brazil are hindered by ideology, stating 'ideology and arithmetic don't mix'. He emphasized the success of private concessions in infrastructure, citing R$390 billion in private investments in the state and advocating for private sector involvement to expand sanitation, highways, and airports.

item.title: Para Tarcísio de Freitas, governo Lula 'não vai deixar saudade'
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) stated that the Lula government 'will not be missed', criticizing the current administration for having missed opportunities during its term. He made the remark during a forum hosted by Veja magazine when asked about the federal government's legacy.

item.title: Moraes rejeita pedido de adiamento e mantém julgamento de Eduardo Bolsonaro nesta terça
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied a request from the Public Defender's Office to postpone the trial of Eduardo Bolsonaro, keeping it scheduled for this Tuesday in the First Chamber. Eduardo Bolsonaro, the former federal deputy and son of ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, is accused of obstructing justice by attempting to impede the investigation into the January 8 coup plot, including seeking U.S. sanctions against Brazilian officials. The charge carries a penalty of 1 to 4 years in prison, with possible increases due to aggravating circumstances.

item.title: BTG/Nexus mostra Lula mais forte e Flávio Bolsonaro mais pressionado pela rejeição
item.description: Lula widened his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round, rising from 40% to 42% and increasing the gap from five to nine points. In the runoff simulation, Lula reached 49% against Flávio’s 43%, strengthening his advantageous position. Both candidates show a consolidated base, with 81% of Lula’s and 77% of Flávio’s supporters saying their vote is decided.
